Governing Instructions: Reviewed repository/Python instructions, development and architecture guidance, and the supplied quality-review contract.

Fail-Fast And Fallback Problems:

  • P2 — Preserve polarization during framework periodic conversion. In _framework.py:991, PeriodicResponse.to_smatrix() constructs SMatrix without retaining tm.polarization. Channels are explicitly generated in that convention at line 969, but SMatrix.__init__ assigns "helicity". A parity unit cell therefore produces parity blocks mislabeled as helicity; subsequent plane-wave scattering, fields, power, and polarization conversion use the wrong convention. The ordinary API preserves it in _physics.py:362. Smallest fix: assign result.polarization = tm.polarization before returning, matching cascade().

Test Quality Problems:

  • Existing periodic framework tests cover only default helicity and miss this defect. Add a parity periodic response comparison against the ordinary API, checking physical scattering/fields and a first-order objective across the three frameworks.

No additional actionable findings in adapter composition, optional dependency declarations, or native gradient ordering inspected. No tests/builds or mutations performed; numerical runtime confirmation remains with the parent.

Original periodic-polarization finding is fixed. cross_widths reuses the existing numerical path, and the SMatrix/ScatteringBlock rename correctly fixes exposed signatures.

Two conversion gaps remain in _framework.py:

  • Backend.polarization_change() calls changepoltype((target, source)) even when conventions match; that primitive rejects identical conventions. Wave, TMatrix, and PortWave.with_polarization(current) consequently raise. Handle this once with an identity transform or return unchanged objects.
  • SMatrix._incident() still directly calls changepoltype, bypassing the new complete-pair validation. Route this conversion through b.polarization_change().
